comparison: Perfect match on C75. Both evaluations support this control experiment showing phenotypes are stress-specific rather than due to general growth defects. OpenEval references CFU data (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), while peer reviewers accept without comment.

Strong agreement on phagosome maturation claims (C87-C92). OpenEval cites confocal microscopy and co-localization data (Figure 4D-F) as supporting evidence. Peer reviewers accept cellular infection results as 'straightforward, internally consistent' and affirm the physiological relevance.

Strong agreement on in vivo virulence claims (C93-C97). OpenEval supports with mouse CFU data (Figure 5A-B). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the in vivo significance, with Reviewer 1 stating the paper 'shows that the increase is important for the survival of the bacterium in animal hosts.'
Both address histopathology claims (C98-C99). OpenEval supports with Figure 5C data. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the broader in vivo evidence without raising concerns.

Strong overlap on PhoP direct binding mechanism (C4, C63, C65-C68). OpenEval cites RT-qPCR, ChIP-qPCR, bioinformatics, and EMSA data (Figure 2B-C, supplements). Peer reviewers provide 'convincing evidence' that PhoP acts as repressor, describing mechanism as 'straightforward' and 'internally consistent.'

Both address PhoR requirement for PhoP-mediated repression (C69-C71, C117). OpenEval supports with RT-qPCR comparing strains with/without PhoR (Figure 3A-B). Peer reviewers affirm the molecular mechanism without challenge.

Partial overlap on PhoP regulation specificity (C2, C58). OpenEval emphasizes RT-qPCR showing specific rv0805 regulation (Figure 2A). Peer reviewers accept PhoP as repressor and note authors 'meticulously responded to all queries' about the mechanism.

Both address specificity of rv0805 regulation by PhoP (C56-C57, C61-C62). OpenEval supports with RT-qPCR data (Figure 2A). Peer reviewers accept specificity while noting a weakness about whether this is the 'only pathway' - acknowledging multiple candidates were examined.

Strong agreement on cAMP measurements (C50-C55). OpenEval cites Figure 1A-B cAMP data, CFU viability, and immunoblotting controls. Peer reviewers accept findings as 'straightforward, internally consistent' and provide 'convincing evidence' for the regulatory mechanism.

Both address cAMP changes due to Rv0805 PDE activity (C72-C74). OpenEval supports with cAMP measurements (Figure 3C) and catalytically inactive mutant controls. Peer reviewers accept that 'cAMP level is increased by decreasing the expression of an enzyme that degrades cAMP.'
Partial overlap on cAMP regulation (C78-C79, C113). OpenEval supports with RT-qPCR and cAMP measurements in knockdown strains (Figure 3D-E). Peer reviewers accept the findings without challenge.

Both address CRISPRi knockdown validation (C76-C77). OpenEval cites Figure 3D-E as orthogonal validation. Peer reviewers accept the specificity of regulation, though note uncertainty about whether this is the exclusive pathway.

Strong overlap on stress tolerance and survival claims (C8-C9, C80-C84, C86, C114). OpenEval supports with growth curves, Alamar Blue, CFU data, and RT-qPCR (Figure 4A-C, supplement 1B). Peer reviewers affirm that 'increases in cAMP level help to increase survival' and describe results as 'straightforward, internally consistent.'

Both address cAMP-dependent effects on stress tolerance (C5-C7). OpenEval emphasizes catalytically inactive mutant controls (Figure 3C, supplement 1A). Peer reviewers affirm the connection between cAMP levels and stress tolerance.

Both address integrated model conclusions (C115, C118). OpenEval describes convergence of multiple experimental approaches supporting the model. Peer reviewers affirm the importance of the findings for understanding Mtb pathogenesis.

Disagreement on phrasing of pathway inactivation claims (C8-C9). OpenEval finds claims supported by experimental data. Peer Reviewer 1 critiques the language as overstated, noting 'genetic manipulation usually means changing DNA' and requesting more fact-based phrasing. The underlying data is not questioned, only the interpretation.

Minimal overlap on C10 (phagosome maturation). OpenEval supports with imaging data. Peer reviewers question the phrasing about 'inactivating the whole pathway' but do not challenge the phagosome maturation data itself.

Both address C85 (lipid biosynthesis gene expression). OpenEval notes this demonstrates phenotypic effects are distinct from broader phoPR-KO defects. Peer reviewers accept this as supporting specificity of the cAMP-mediated mechanism.
